symbols.name: \(\Delta_{\mathrm{lift}}(P)\)
symbols.def: The minimum of \(\operatorname{dist}(a_p,\partial[-1/2,1/2]^2)\), \(\operatorname{dist}(a_T,\partial[-1/2,1/2]^2)\), \(\inf_x\operatorname{dist}((x,p(x)),\operatorname{Cut}_{\mathbb T})\), and \(\inf_y\operatorname{dist}((y,T(y)),\operatorname{Cut}_{\mathbb T})\).

symbols.name: \(\operatorname{Disp}_{\mathbb T}\)
symbols.def: If \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}(F)=(a_F,\phi_F,\widetilde F)\), define \(\operatorname{Disp}_{\mathbb T}(F,y)=\widetilde y-\widetilde F(\widetilde y)=-a_F-\nabla\phi_F(\widetilde y)\); equivariance makes the value independent of the representative \(\widetilde y\) of \(y\), and the fixed Borel fallback makes the functional total.

symbols.name: \(\alpha\)

symbols.name: \(B\)

symbols.name: \(\mathsf C\)
symbols.def: The pulled-back inner coefficient \(\mathsf C=\det(D)D^{-1}A(R_0)D^{-\mathsf T}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal H_P\)
symbols.def: For a regular path \(P_t\) with tangent \(\delta\), let \(\dot a_p=\partial_t a_{p_t}|_{t=0}\) and \(\dot a_T=\partial_t a_{T_t}|_{t=0}\) be the translations selected by \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}\), and set \(\mathcal H_P[\delta]=(\dot a_T-\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot\dot a_p])_{\mathcal Y_J}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal D_P\)

symbols.name: \(\widetilde f_g\)

symbols.name: \(\widehat f_g\)

symbols.name: \(\Psi_{g,h}\)

symbols.name: \(\theta_n\)

symbols.name: \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^{R}\)

symbols.name: \(\widehat c_{1-\gamma}\)

symbols.name: \(\mathcal E_j\)

novel.justification: This intrinsic flat-torus production model is newly maintained rather than inherited from the Euclidean changes-in-changes theorem. It is realistic for genuinely periodic bivariate outcomes, including seasonal phase pairs and directional coordinates, and it is satisfied by smooth equivariant gradient production maps with positive Jacobian margins.

novel.justification: This open separation condition excludes only maps whose selected harmonic translation lies on a lattice branch boundary or whose transport graph touches the squared-distance cut locus. It is stable under small \(C^1\) perturbations and is satisfied by smooth periodic displacement fields whose coordinate displacements stay strictly inside one injectivity cell, including the explicit separable witness.

This synchronized bandwidth regime is newly maintained for the nested two-dimensional functional: it balances the order-minus-two transport bias, the \(C^{2,1/4}\) pilot stability needed along the nonlinear interpolation, and the quadratic \(C^{1,1/4}\) remainder. Polynomial choices in this interval are implementable without oracle quantities, and for the maintained \(s\geq8\) class the interval is nonempty.

standard.name: Interior-point condition for local minimax analysis

definitions.name: \(\mathcal F_s\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal F_s=\{P=(P_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}:P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CiC}}^{\mathrm{per}}\text{ and ass:density-positivity, ass:density-smoothness, ass:inner-ellipticity, ass:outer-ellipticity, and ass:lift-regularity hold}\}\).

definitions.name: Measurable translation-aware equivariant lift
definitions.construction: For each regular identity-homotopic torus optimal-transport diffeomorphism \(F\), choose the unique triple \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}(F)=(a_F,\phi_F,\widetilde F)\) such that \(a_F\in\mathcal Q\), \(\int_{\mathbb T^2}\phi_F=0\), and \(\widetilde F(x)=x+a_F+\nabla\phi_F(x)\) is \(\mathbb Z^2\)-equivariant. Extend this selector measurably to all map estimates by the fixed fallback \((0,0,\operatorname{id})\) off the regular domain, and define \(\operatorname{Disp}_{\mathbb T}(F,y)=-a_F-\nabla\phi_F(\widetilde y)\).

definitions.name: Nested Brenier changes-in-changes functional
definitions.construction: \(p=\operatorname{OT}(P_{C0},P_{C1}),\ q=p\#P_{T0},\ T=\operatorname{OT}(P_{T1},q)\). Select \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}(p)=(a_p,\phi_p,\widetilde p)\) and \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}(T)=(a_T,\phi_T,\widetilde T)\), and set \(\tau(P)=(-a_T-\nabla\phi_T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J=(\operatorname{Disp}_{\mathbb T}(T,y_j))_{j=1}^J\).

definitions.name: Order-s positive-normalized periodized KDE
definitions.construction: For every \(g\in\mathcal G\), set \(\widetilde f_g(x)=n_g^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}K_{h_n}^{\mathrm{per}}(x-X_{g,i})\) and \(\widehat f_g(x)=\max\{c/2,\widetilde f_g(x)\}/\int_{\mathbb T^2}\max\{c/2,\widetilde f_g(u)\}\,du\).

definitions.name: Nested KDE and Monge--Ampere plug-in
definitions.construction: Compute \(\widehat p=\operatorname{OT}(\widehat P_{C0},\widehat P_{C1})\), select \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}(\widehat p)=(\widehat a_p,\widehat\phi_p,\widetilde{\widehat p})\), form \(\widehat q=\widehat p\#\widehat P_{T0}\) through \(\widehat f_q(z)=\widehat f_{C1}(z)(\widehat f_{T0}/\widehat f_{C0})(\widehat p^{-1}(z))\), compute \(\widehat T=\operatorname{OT}(\widehat P_{T1},\widehat q)\), select \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}(\widehat T)=(\widehat a_T,\widehat\phi_T,\widetilde{\widehat T})\), and return \(\widehat\tau=(-\widehat a_T-\nabla\widehat\phi_T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\). The half-open-cell selector is used on its regular domain and the fixed Borel fallback from \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}\) otherwise.

definitions.name: Pulled-coordinate nested derivative
definitions.construction:

definitions.name: Full four-cell finite-bandwidth covariance
definitions.construction: For each cell, insert the centered kernel tangent in def:nested-derivative to obtain \(\Psi_{g,h}\), retaining the harmonic translation score, both appearances of every control noise, and all within-cell cross products, and set \(\Sigma_h(P)=\log(1/h)^{-1}\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\rho_g^{-1}\operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi_{g,h}(X))\).

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{crit}}\)
definitions.construction: Pull both inner and generated-pushforward equations into treated-post coordinates using def:nested-derivative; retain the harmonic projection \(\mathcal H_P\); freeze only \(B\) at each Green pole; subtract the anisotropic logarithmic fundamental solution with a smooth cutoff; split the smoothed response into radii below a fixed multiple of \(h_n\), between that radius and a fixed positive radius, and outside that radius; control coefficient, generated-target, moving-pole, lift-branch, and harmonic-score errors with weighted Schauder estimates; and close the stochastic expansion with a quadratic \(C^{1,1/4}\) remainder under a small \(C^{2,1/4}\) perturbation.

definitions.name: Cross-fitted adjoint covariance estimator
definitions.construction: Split every cell into two deterministic folds; on the opposite fold estimate all densities, maps, selected lift translations and potentials, coefficients, and poles; compute the finite-bandwidth harmonic translation score and solve the adjoints of the two elliptic inverses in def:nested-derivative against each coordinate evaluation; add these components before evaluating and centering \(\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}\) on fold \(r\); assemble \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}\) by its displayed weighted empirical covariance formula; and set \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^{R}=\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}+\theta_n I_{2J}\) with \(\theta_n=n^{-1}\).

definitions.name: Simultaneous multiplier ellipses
definitions.construction: Generate independent \(\xi_{g,i}\), compute \(Z^\star\), take \(\widehat c_{1-\gamma}\in[0,\infty)\) as the conditional quantile of \(\max_{1\le j\le J}(Z_j^\star)^{\mathsf T}(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj},jj}^{R})^{-1}Z_j^\star\), and return \(\mathcal E_j=\{u\in\mathbb R^2:(n/L_n)(\widehat\tau_j-u)^{\mathsf T}(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj},jj}^{R})^{-1}(\widehat\tau_j-u)\le\widehat c_{1-\gamma}\}\) for \(1\leq j\leq J\).

definitions.name: Green-aligned multiscale product-Hellinger alternatives
definitions.construction: Set \(\varepsilon_n=n^{-\eta}\). For \(g=g_\star\), define \[f_{n,\pm,g_\star}=f_{0g_\star}\left(1\pm\frac{\zeta\,\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}}{\sqrt n\,\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}\rVert_{L^2(P_{0g_\star})}}\right),\] and for every \(g\neq g_\star\) set \(f_{n,\pm,g}=f_{0g}\); let \(P_{n,+}\) and \(P_{n,-}\) be the corresponding four-law tuples.

definitions.name: Smooth nonzero-effect separable torus witness
definitions.construction: Take \(U\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\mathbb T^2)\), \(h_0^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)=u\), \(h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)=(u_1+0.1\sin(2\pi u_1)/\pi,u_2)\), \(h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)=(u_1+0.15\sin(2\pi u_1)/\pi,u_2-0.05\sin(2\pi u_2)/\pi)\), and let \(P^{\mathrm{sep}}\) be the four induced laws.

statements.statement: For every representation satisfying ass:cic-identification, uniqueness of absolutely continuous optimal transport on \(\mathbb T^2\) for the cost \(c_{\mathbb T}\) gives \(p=h_1\circ h_0^{-1}\) \(P_{C0}\)-almost everywhere, \(q=h_1\#\nu_T\), and \(T=h_1\circ h_{1\star}^{-1}\) \(P_{T1}\)-almost everywhere. Under ass:lift-regularity, \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}(p)=(a_p,\phi_p,\widetilde p)\) and \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}(T)=(a_T,\phi_T,\widetilde T)\) select locally stable branches, and the no-treatment treated-post displacement is identified as \(\tau(P)=(-a_T-\nabla\phi_T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\).
statements.justification: The lemma supplies the missing intrinsic torus identification step before any statistical argument uses the nested Brenier functional.
statements.gap: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC proves a Euclidean cyclic-comonotonicity result; it does not prove this intrinsic squared-geodesic torus statement or the translation-aware selected-lift displacement conclusion.
statements.consumer: The lemma makes the smooth periodic analytic model a causal model rather than an unsupported transfer of a Euclidean theorem.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal F_s\) and smooth four-density path with tangent \(\delta\), the selected lifted map \(P\mapsto(\widetilde T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\) is Frechet differentiable and its derivative is exactly \(\mathcal D_P[\delta]=\mathcal H_P[\delta]+ ig(
abla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})+e_{T0}-e_{T1}]-
abla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[(\mathsf C
abla\alpha)\cdot
abla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}(e_{C1}-e_{C0})] ig)_{\mathcal Y_J}\), where \(\mathcal H_P[\delta]=(\dot a_T-
abla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[(\mathsf C
abla\alpha)\cdot\dot a_p])_{\mathcal Y_J}\), \(\dot a_p=\partial_t a_{p_t}|_{t=0}\), and \(\dot a_T=\partial_t a_{T_t}|_{t=0}\). The coefficient multiplying the pulled-back inner equation satisfies \(B D^{-\mathsf T}=\alpha\mathsf C\). The map \(\delta\mapsto(\dot a_p,\dot a_T)\) has cellwise Riesz scores with uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\) norms. Consequently \(\mathcal H_P\) contributes \(O(1/\log(1/h))\) to \(\Sigma_h(P)\), and its cross-covariance with the Green score is \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\), both uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\). This strictly extends the one-target density-curve derivative in GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization to a four-input nested map with a generated target law and nonzero harmonic translation modes.
statements.justification: The identity exposes every generated-target path, separates the bounded harmonic translation mode, and reduces the singular part to one outer elliptic inverse.
statements.gap: GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization differentiates one target-density curve with a fixed source; it does not differentiate an outer map whose target is itself an estimated pushforward through an inner map.
statements.consumer: The exact weights determine which of the four Card--Krueger cells drives uncertainty in each bivariate counterfactual arrow.

statements.statement: For the order-\(s\) KDE and the tame nonlinear expansion with Holder index \(1/4\), the three exact scale requirements are \[\sqrt{n/L_n}\,h_n^{s-2}\to0,\qquad \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{13/2}}}+h_n^{s-9/4}\to0,\qquad \sqrt{n/L_n}\left(\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{9/2}}}+h_n^{s-5/4}\right)^2\to0.\] They are respectively the order-minus-two deterministic bias bound, the \(C^{2,1/4}\) stochastic-pilot smallness bound, and the quadratic \(C^{1,1/4}\) remainder bound. Under \(h_n=n^{-a_h}\), \(L_n=a_h\log n\), and \(s\geq8\), their conjunction holds exactly for \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/9\): the pilot stochastic term only requires \(a_h<2/13\), the stochastic square requires \(a_h<1/9\), the bias permits equality at \(a_h=1/[2(s-2)]\), and the pilot-bias, squared-bias, and mixed terms then vanish.
statements.justification: The lemma exposes every exponent constraint used by the critical expansion and certifies the maximal polynomial window delivered by the stated tame norms.
statements.gap: ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT does not derive this three-way bandwidth balance for a nested generated-target functional in dimension two.
statements.consumer: The exact window lets implementations select bandwidths without an unexplained safety exponent and lets the critical-limit proof audit each bias and stochastic remainder separately.

statements.statement: Can the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{crit}}\) establish, uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\), that the variable-coefficient smoothed gradient Green response has the frozen-pole logarithmic covariance, that the second elliptic term of \(\mathcal D_P\) and its harmonic term \(\mathcal H_P\) have bounded \(L^2\) scores, that coefficient, pole, and selected-lift plug-in errors are \(o(L_n^{1/2})\) in score norm, and that the nonlinear nested remainder is \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n/n})\)?
statements.justification: This is the first-class open analytic content; without all four controls, the proposed covariance and feasible inference are unsupported.
statements.gap: ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT reports that its coefficient-freezing error is of leading order in dimension two. Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 of GonzalezSanzShengWuAvellaMedina2026Influence prove the contamination Green response and pole singularity, but not the shrinking-bandwidth nested stochastic remainder.
statements.consumer: A positive resolution supplies the reusable critical-plane module needed by every subsequent limit, covariance, and lower-bound theorem in the project.

statements.statement: For the full scores from def:full-score-covariance, including the harmonic translation score and the covariance between the leading and generated-target responses within each control cell, \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\lVert\Sigma_{h_n}(P)-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\), where \(V(P)=\operatorname{diag}(V_1,\ldots,V_J)\), \(V_j=w_j\sqrt{\det H(y_j)}H(y_j)/(4\pi f_{T1}(y_j))\), and \(w_j=\alpha(y_j)(\rho_{C0}^{-1}+\rho_{C1}^{-1})+\rho_{T0}^{-1}+\rho_{T1}^{-1}\). The normalized harmonic variance and every Green--harmonic cross-covariance vanish by the uniform \(L^2\) bound in thm:nested-derivative.
statements.justification: The closed form records the exact cell weights and shows why independent-cell noise cannot cancel the critical logarithm.
statements.gap: ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT gives a one-sample uniform-law dimension-two block and no generated-target paths; the displayed covariance is four-sample, variable-coefficient, and nested.
statements.consumer: The block matrices provide interpretable standard-error diagnostics and an independent check on the adjoint numerical implementation.

statements.statement: Under the stated four-sample design, \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}d_{\mathrm{BL}}(\mathcal L_P[\sqrt{n/L_n}(\widehat\tau-\tau(P))],N(0,V(P)))\to0\). Uniform map consistency and ass:lift-regularity imply that the half-open-cell lift branch is selected for both \(\widehat p\) and \(\widehat T\) with probability \(1-o(1)\), uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\); hence the measurable fallback has probability \(o(1)\) and does not alter the limit. This strictly extends the uniform-to-uniform, fixed-source dimension-two conclusion of Proposition 29 in ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT to general variable coefficients and to the four-input nested causal functional.
statements.justification: The limit law turns the identified multivariate changes-in-changes map into an inferential object at the two-dimensional critical rate.
statements.gap: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC stops at consistency, and ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT explicitly leaves general-density dimension two open.
statements.consumer: Applied researchers can attach uncertainty to the full-time versus part-time employment displacement vectors in a prespecified smooth Card--Krueger reanalysis.

statements.statement: The estimator in def:adjoint-covariance retains the finite-bandwidth harmonic translation score and every generated-target cross product and satisfies \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P(\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon)\to0\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P(\lVert\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^{R}-V(P)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon)\to0\) for every \(\varepsilon>0\). The harmonic variance and its Green cross-covariances vanish after division by \(L_n\), but retaining them makes the finite-bandwidth covariance exact. Uniform positive definiteness of \(V(P)\), covariance consistency, and \(\theta_n=n^{-1}\) imply \(\max_{1\le j\le J}\lVert(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj},jj}^{R})^{-1}-V_j(P)^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), so the ridge is asymptotically negligible while every block inverse exists in every sample.
statements.justification: A covariance formula is operational only if the unknown elliptic coefficients, pullbacks, and moving poles can be estimated on the critical scale.
statements.gap: GonzalezSanzMordantSheng2026PotentialFCLT uses adjoints for bounded weighted potential contrasts and explicitly excludes pointwise gradients; this result handles singular gradient evaluations and nesting.
statements.consumer: The estimator supplies standard errors for a reproducible Card--Krueger arrow plot and detects whether control-cell uncertainty was incorrectly omitted.

statements.statement: For every finite sample, \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^{R}\) is positive definite, all block inverses in def:multiplier-ellipses exist, and the conditional critical value \(\widehat c_{1-\gamma}\) is well defined in \([0,\infty)\). Conditionally on the data, \(Z^\star\) consistently estimates the law of \(\sqrt{n/L_n}(\widehat\tau-\tau(P))\), and the ridged ellipses obey \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\{\tau_j(P)\in\mathcal E_j\text{ for all }1\leq j\leq J\}\to1-\gamma\).
statements.justification: Joint vector ellipses preserve the direction and covariance of each employment substitution arrow while controlling multiplicity across the fixed grid.
statements.gap: PonnopratOkanoImaizumi2024UniformBand obtains one-dimensional quantile-map bands; no published result gives simultaneous fixed-grid ellipses for a continuous bivariate nested map.
statements.consumer: The ellipses allow the Card--Krueger reanalysis to distinguish a joint full-time and part-time substitution pattern from coordinatewise noise.

statements.statement: There are constants \(c_1,c_2,C,\zeta_0>0\), uniform over admissible interior centers, such that \(c_1\log(1/\varepsilon)\leq\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\rVert_{L^2(P_{0g_\star})}^2\leq c_2\log(1/\varepsilon)\) and \(\lVert f_{0g_\star}\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\rVert_{C^s}\leq C\varepsilon^{-s-1}\). For every fixed \(0<\zeta\leq\zeta_0\) satisfying \(C\zeta^2\leq\kappa\), the explicit laws from def:green-local-alternatives obey \(P_{n,+},P_{n,-}\in\mathcal F_s\cap\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa)\), \[\operatorname{Hel}^2\left(\bigotimes_{g\in\mathcal G}P_{n,+,g}^{\otimes n_g},\bigotimes_{g\in\mathcal G}P_{n,-,g}^{\otimes n_g}\right)\leq C\zeta^2\leq1/2,\] and \[\left|\upsilon^{\mathsf T}\{\tau(P_{n,+})-\tau(P_{n,-})\}_1\right|\geq c_1\zeta\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}{n}}.\] The restriction \(\eta<1/[2(s+1)]\) makes the \(C^s\) perturbation \(O(n^{-1/2}\varepsilon_n^{-s-1}/\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)})\) vanish, and perturbing the cell with \(n_{g_\star}=n\) makes the product-Hellinger bound independent of the other cell-size ratios. For each sign, write \(p\) and \(T\) for the inner and outer optimal maps evaluated at \(P_{n,\pm}\), with translations and potentials selected by \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}\). Causal-class membership is witnessed constructively by \(h_0=\operatorname{id}\), \(\nu_C=P_{n,\pm,C0}\), \(\nu_T=P_{n,\pm,T0}\), \(h_1=p\), and \(h_{1\star}=T^{-1}\circ p\); torus optimal-transport uniqueness makes the two required compositions \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone. The vanishing \(C^s\) perturbation and interior margins imply that \(p\), \(T\), and \(T^{-1}\circ p\) remain diffeomorphisms, preserve the ellipticity bounds, remain on the same half-open lift branches, and stay a fixed positive distance from the squared-distance cut locus for all sufficiently large \(n\). Moreover \(\lVert a_p(P_{n,\pm})-a_p(P_0)\rVert+\lVert a_T(P_{n,\pm})-a_T(P_0)\rVert=O(n^{-1/2})\); thus the harmonic translation changes are negligible relative to the Green separation \(\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)/n}\).
statements.justification: The lemma audits the converse through a named annular Green tangent, normalized alternatives, class membership, bounded product-experiment distance, and a quantitative estimand separation.
statements.gap: The single-scale Fano perturbations in HutterRigollet2021Minimax control global map loss but do not accumulate the pointwise logarithm or coordinate four unequal samples through product Hellinger distance.
statements.consumer: The explicit two-point experiment turns the critical logarithm into a checkable information bound for the nested displacement rather than a heuristic variance analogy.

statements.statement: There are constants \(C_1,c_0,\kappa>0\) such that \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb E_P\lVert\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\rVert^2\leq C_1L_n/n\) and \(\liminf_{n\to\infty}(n/L_n)\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa)}\mathbb E_P\lVert\widetilde\tau_n-\tau(P)\rVert^2\geq c_0\). The lower bound is witnessed by def:green-local-alternatives and lem:green-local-alternatives, for which \(\log(1/\varepsilon_n)=(\eta/a_h)L_n\).
statements.justification: The Green-aligned two-point converse certifies that the logarithmic critical variance is information-theoretic rather than a defect of the chosen smoother.
statements.gap: HutterRigollet2021Minimax and ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2024Plugin study global one-map loss; their dimension-two lower bound does not produce the pointwise logarithm or a nested four-cell local experiment.
statements.consumer: The rate certificate tells users that reducing the Card--Krueger arrow uncertainty requires more information or structure, not merely a different smooth plug-in implementation.

statements.statement: If all four cell densities are uniform, then \(p=T=R_0=\operatorname{id}\), \(\alpha=1\), \(\mathcal D_P[\delta]=\nabla(-\Delta)^{-1}(-\delta_{C0}+\delta_{C1}+\delta_{T0}-\delta_{T1})\), and equal cell sizes give \(V_j=I_2/\pi\). In the fixed-source subexperiment with only \(P_{T1}\) sampled, the covariance reduces to \(I_2/(4\pi)\), exactly the known uniform dimension-two result.
statements.justification: The reduction is an auditable sign, scale, and angular-constant check for the nested formula.
statements.gap: ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT proves the final one-cell reduction but does not derive the four-cell \(I_2/\pi\) nested covariance.
statements.consumer: The identity is a unit test for Fourier and adjoint solvers before the nonconstant-coefficient experiment is attempted.

statements.statement: For constants whose bounds contain the displayed Jacobian ranges and for \(\beta\) below the displayed displacement and cut-locus margins, the construction in def:separable-witness satisfies \(P^{\mathrm{sep}}\in\mathcal F_s\). The translation coordinates in the three triples returned by \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathbb T}\) are zero; the potential coordinates for \(h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\) and \(h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}\) are respectively \(-0.1\cos(2\pi u_1)/(2\pi^2)\) and \(-0.15\cos(2\pi u_1)/(2\pi^2)+0.05\cos(2\pi u_2)/(2\pi^2)\). At \(u=(1/4,1/4)\) and \(y=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)\), its translation-aware displacement is \(\operatorname{Disp}_{\mathbb T}(T,y)=(0.05/\pi,-0.05/\pi)\neq0\), its outer Jacobian is positive definite, and equal cell sizes give \(V_j=I_2/\pi\).
statements.justification: The witness proves nonemptiness with a nonzero causal arrow and avoids relying only on the identity-map law.
statements.gap: The available uniform-law calculation has zero displacement; this witness keeps the critical constant while producing a genuine bivariate effect.
statements.consumer: The witness supplies the first reproducible analytic benchmark for the proposed nonseparable numerical kill test and for software validation.

sampling_model.design: Four mutually independent repeated-cross-section samples indexed by \(g\in\{C0,C1,T0,T1\}\).
sampling_model.units: Within cell \(g\), \(X_{g,1},\ldots,X_{g,n_g}\) are independent draws from \(P_g\), with \(n=\min_g n_g\) and \(n_g/n\to\rho_g\).
sampling_model.treatment: The treatment group is untreated at period zero and exposed at period one; the intrinsic torus changes-in-changes lemma identifies the no-treatment treated-post map from invertible production maps and two \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone graphs.
sampling_model.overlap: Every cell density is bounded between \(c\) and \(C\) on \(\mathbb T^2\), both nested Brenier Jacobians are uniformly elliptic, and the selected population lift branches remain \(\beta\)-separated from lattice boundaries and the squared-distance cut locus.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each cell density uses the order-\(s\) signed periodized KDE followed by clipping at \(c/2\) and mass renormalization. The half-open-cell lift selector returns \(\widehat a_p,\widehat\phi_p,\widehat a_T,\widehat\phi_T\) and uses a fixed measurable fallback off its regular domain. Covariance pilots are two-fold cross-fitted, include the harmonic translation score, and are evaluated by adjoint elliptic solves; \(n^{-1}I_{2J}\) is added before every block inversion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 29 proves a \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) pointwise Gaussian limit with covariance \(I_2/(4\pi)\) only when source and target are uniform on \(\mathbb T^2\).
Theorem 3.2 differentiates a Brenier map along one smooth target-density curve through a linearized Monge--Ampere boundary problem.

Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 identify the multivariate changes-in-changes counterfactual law and map under cyclic comonotonicity, while the estimation section gives consistency rather than a sampling law.

Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 identify the gradient-Green contamination influence and its pole singularity; the abstract reports numerical stable-type fluctuations but the paper does not prove a shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical central limit theorem.
Theorems 2.4 and 2.10 give a weak functional limit and bootstrap for empirical Brenier potentials and fixed weighted contrasts, not pointwise gradients.
Theorems 2 and 6 give near-matching global \(L^2\) minimax rates for one smooth transport map through wavelet semi-dual estimation and a Fano lower bound.
Theorem 18 gives the \(\log n/n\) global squared-risk upper rate for a two-dimensional smooth density plug-in map without a matching logarithmic lower bound.
Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 validate a smoothed bootstrap uniform band for a one-dimensional quantile-represented transport map.

Theorems 2--4 and Corollary 2 derive efficient influence functions and root-\(n\) cross-fitted inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional estimands under a distributional bridge in paired panel data.

tldr: An intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes lemma identifies the translation-aware displacement of a nested Brenier counterfactual from invertible production maps and two \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone graphs. A half-open-cell selector writes each regular equivariant lift as \(x+a_F+\nabla\phi_F(x)\), while an open branch-margin condition and a measurable fallback make the target and estimator total. The project derives the exact four-input derivative including its harmonic translation mode, proves a general-density critical-plane Gaussian law for a specified positive-normalized periodized-KDE plug-in at rate \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) under \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/9\), retains all finite-bandwidth cross terms, estimates them by cross-fitted adjoint solves, calibrates ridge-regularized fixed-grid ellipses, and matches the \(\log(1/h_n)/n\) squared-risk scale by explicit Green-aligned product-Hellinger alternatives.

project_justification.gap: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC motivates cyclic-comonotone changes-in-changes in Euclidean outcome spaces but does not prove the intrinsic squared-geodesic torus identification lemma; SunTchetgenTchetgen2025DebiasedCiC gives orthogonal efficient inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional effects under a distributional bridge, not for a bivariate Brenier-map displacement under cyclic comonotonicity; ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT proves the relevant smooth-map pointwise limit for \(d\geq3\) and only the uniform-to-uniform special case for \(d=2\); the 2026 Green-influence and potential-limit papers still do not establish a pointwise gradient law with a generated target.
project_justification.niche: In the critical plane, a Green gradient has logarithmically divergent variance, while nesting makes the same control noises enter the outer target through more than one path. This creates a distinct four-sample covariance and a nonregular local information problem.
project_justification.fill: An intrinsic torus identification lemma first turns the periodic model into a causal model. A translation-aware measurable lift separates the harmonic vector \(a_F\) from the mean-zero potential \(\phi_F\). The exact pulled-coordinate derivative then identifies one leading outer Green response to four weighted empirical processes, one smoother generated-target response, and a bounded harmonic translation response. A pole parametrix, an exponent-audited tame nonlinear expansion, cross-fitted adjoint covariance with asymptotically negligible deterministic ridge, and explicitly normalized annular Green alternatives yield a joint limit, total simultaneous inference, and a matched local minimax rate.

related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC motivates the production-function and cyclic-comonotonicity structure in Euclidean outcome spaces and the Card--Krueger application. McCann2001PolarFactorization supplies existence and almost-everywhere uniqueness of squared-distance optimal maps from absolutely continuous laws on compact Riemannian manifolds. The intrinsic cost \(c_{\mathbb T}(x,y)=d_{\mathbb T^2}(x,y)^2/2\), torus changes-in-changes identification step, and translation-aware selection \(\widetilde F(x)=x+a_F+\nabla\phi_F(x)\) are new here: the Euclidean changes-in-changes theorem does not prove this transfer, and Euclidean cyclic monotonicity of an arbitrary periodic lift is not equated with \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclic monotonicity. Its target and assumptions are strictly non-overlapping with the present fixed-grid bivariate Brenier-map displacement under cyclic comonotonicity: neither result subsumes the other. ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT supplies the periodized KDE and quantitative Monge--Ampere linearization, proves the uniform dimension-two special case, and explicitly leaves general variable coefficients open. PonnopratOkanoImaizumi2024UniformBand motivates simultaneous transport-map uncertainty in one dimension, while the present ellipse problem requires singular bivariate adjoints.
technical_internal_limitation: The decisive analytic risk is uniform control of the variable-coefficient pole after transformed KDE smoothing. Before broad proof development, evaluate one nonseparable smooth torus law with nonconstant \(f_{T0}/f_{C0}\) at bandwidths \(h,h/2,h/4,h/8\), refine the PDE mesh until discretization changes are negligible, compare each cellwise covariance increment with \(V(P)\), and separately track the generated-target and harmonic-translation remainders. A persistent slope discrepancy, a logarithmically divergent remainder, or nonvanishing normalized Green--harmonic cross-covariance invalidates the proposed spine. The local converse must separately verify the two-sided \(L^2\) logarithmic norm and \(C^s\) envelope for \(\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\), positivity and normalization of both displayed alternatives, constructive membership in the intrinsic torus cyclic-comonotone class, preservation of diffeomorphism, ellipticity, lift-branch, and cut-locus margins, the \(O(n^{-1/2})\) translation change, bounded product-Hellinger distance for the least-sampled cell, first-order Green separation, and negligibility of the nonlinear remainder. The cutoff \(\varepsilon_n=n^{-\eta}\) is independent of \(h_n\); substituting \(\varepsilon_n=h_n\) is not licensed.
honest_scope: The intrinsic torus identification lemma is a contribution: the Euclidean changes-in-changes paper motivates the model but does not establish a flat-torus specialization. The target uses the unique half-open-cell translation \(a_T\) and mean-zero potential \(\phi_T\); it does not impose zero flux. Population inner and outer maps are maintained a fixed positive distance from the lattice branch boundary and the squared-distance cut locus. The estimator uses the same selector with a measurable fallback whose probability is \(o(1)\) by uniform consistency. The theorem concerns a fixed separated grid, independent repeated cross sections, positive smooth torus densities, the polynomial window \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/9\), and uniformly elliptic maps; it is not a confidence band and does not cover paired panels, vanishing densities, growing grids, branch-crossing sequences, or raw discrete counts. The endpoint \(a_h=1/[2(s-2)]\) is included because the remaining factor \(1/\sqrt{\log n}\) makes the deterministic bias negligible, whereas \(a_h=1/9\) is excluded because the stochastic quadratic remainder retains a \(\sqrt{\log n}\) factor. The exact derivative includes the harmonic translation term, although its bounded score has vanishing normalized variance and Green cross-covariance. Raw empirical covariance blocks may be singular, so every finite-sample ellipse uses \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}^{R}=\widehat V_{\mathrm{adj}}+n^{-1}I_{2J}\); its conditional critical value may equal zero, and its asymptotic equivalence follows from covariance consistency and uniform positive definiteness of \(V(P)\). Card--Krueger employment counts do not literally satisfy the smooth model, so the empirical target must be declared in advance as a smoothed exploratory estimand and reported with regularization sensitivity. The local minimax claim is over genuinely two-dimensional perturbations whose causal-class membership and lift-branch stability are witnessed constructively. When only the treated-post law is sampled and all laws are uniform, the result reduces to Proposition 29 of ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT; when all four cells are sampled equally, it yields the four-noise covariance \(I_2/\pi\).

SunTchetgenTchetgen2025DebiasedCiC takes a different CiC route: its Theorems 2--4 and Corollary 2 develop Neyman-orthogonal efficient inference for scalar ATT and scalar distributional estimands from paired panels under a distributional bridge. That scalar bridge model neither supplies nor is supplied by cyclic comonotonicity for a bivariate Brenier map. ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT supplies the same periodized KDE and quantitative Monge--Ampere linearization, but its general theorem starts at \(d=3\); Proposition 29 proves only the uniform \(d=2\) case, and Section 6 states that its general coefficient-freezing error is of leading order. GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization establishes smooth single-map target-path differentiation through an elliptic equation, not a generated pushforward or a torus harmonic translation mode. The arXiv:2607.19080v1 abstract of GonzalezSanzShengWuAvellaMedina2026Influence reports numerical stable-type fluctuations, and Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 prove the Green contamination influence and pole singularity; it does not prove a shrinking-bandwidth nested empirical central limit theorem. GonzalezSanzMordantSheng2026PotentialFCLT proves a weak potential limit and bootstrap for bounded weighted contrasts and explicitly excludes map-gradient inference.
